info.title: Switch Library Manager Web API
info.description: Read the library, its statistics and download files. When a login is required (users exist, or SLM_AUTH_USERNAME / SLM_AUTH_PASSWORD is set), every endpoint except /healthz needs an API key (`Authorization: Bearer slm_...`, made in My account), HTTP basic authentication or a session cookie. A key does at most what its user does, and a read-only key only looks and downloads. Read-only users can call the GET endpoints; changes need an administrator. Requests that change data are rejected when they come from another web site; requests without browser headers (curl, scripts, Home Assistant) are accepted.

get.description: All base games of the library by title ID, with their latest local update and DLC.

get.summary: What was changed of a game by hand
get.description: The name, cover and description an administrator gave the game on its page. They win over the titles database, its translations, the files of the game and IGDB, in every language. An update or DLC ID tells its game.

200.description: The changes; edited is false when there are none

404.description: Neither the titles database nor the library knows the game

post.summary: Change the name, cover or description of a game
post.description: Kept apart from the titles database, by title ID, so synchronizations and scans never lose it; the files of the game and its title ID are not touched, and Organize uses the name given when it runs. The name and the description sent replace the ones kept (empty: those of the game). A cover sent, as a file or as an address downloaded once, replaces the one kept; without one the cover kept stays. Covers must be JPEG, PNG or GIF images of at most 5 MB and 6000 pixels a side; they are made again, at most 1024 pixels a side. When nothing is left the change is forgotten.

post.summary: Find the cover of a game in the eShop
post.description: Searches the eShop of Europe by the name of a game, without the marks of file names ([title ID], [v0], the extension), for administrators. It gives the games with a square image of 500×500 (at most 24) and the address of a search of images on the web for the same name; the image chosen is then sent as the coverUrl of the change of a game.

The API keys of the user who asks, the newest first. The keys themselves are never sent again, only their last characters. An administrator gets the keys of every user with all=true.

post.description: A key for the user who asks, signed in with a session or a password: a key cannot make keys. The key is in this answer only and cannot be shown again; only a hash of it is kept. It never does more than its user does at the time: when the role of the user is lowered, the key does less too, and the keys of a deleted user go with them. A user has at most 20 keys.

post.summary: Remove a game from a console
post.description: Asks a console of the user to remove a game installed on it: it waits with what is sent to the console (GET /install/push/wait), as an item with action remove, the title ID of the game and its name (game). NXDock asks on the console before removing it and copies its saves to the library first; it answers on POST /install/push/answer with accepted and, when it accepted, result: removed, failed or missing (it was not installed). Asked again before the console answers, it is not asked twice. Noted in the activity, and so is the answer.

post.summary: What is installed on a console (NXDock)
post.description: Sent by NXDock with the key of the console, when its user agrees: replaces what it told before. Only with the network install on, and on the local network unless allowed. The titles told wrong or twice are left out; a system told wrong refuses the whole request. The minutes played are also kept once a day, for 400 days. {"off": true} forgets all of it.

403.description: Not the key of a console, or from outside the local network

413.description: More than 5000 titles, or titles played

post.description: A report of what went wrong on the console, sent by NXDock with the key of the console: a ZIP of at most 16 MiB and 200 files, whose names are relative and stay inside it (no symbolic links). Kept for the administrators; the newest 10 of each console stay. Noted in the activity.

id.description: One or several title IDs (repeat the field)

post.summary: Mark a game you have without its file
post.description: Marks a game you have without a file of it in the library (a game card, for instance), for the whole library, or takes the mark away. A marked game shows in the library as a game without a file and is not listed or counted as missing; its updates and DLC are not counted. Marking a game takes it off the wishlist. Needs an editor or an administrator.

id.description: The title ID of the game (not of an update or a DLC)

owned.description: true marks the game, false takes the mark away

400.description: Invalid title ID, or not the ID of a game

post.description: Checks the files of the library in the background, at a level: signature reads the header of every NCA and tells in seconds whether it has the signature of Nintendo; hash reads every file whole and checks every NCA against its hashes; both does the two, the hashes even when the signature fails. A file whose data does not match its hashes is failed; a file with an NCA not signed by Nintendo and nothing damaged is modified, which is no failure. The results are listed on the Issues page and in the task (GET /api/tasks). If a task works on the files, the check waits in the queue.

all.description: true checks every file again; false only the new and changed ones

200.description: Nothing to check: no file is new or changed since its last check at this level

202.description: Started, or added to the queue

get.description: Synchronizations, scans and organize runs, newest first. Failed tasks stay until they are dismissed.
Sends an event `tasks` with the version of the task list right away and after every change (at most twice a second), and a comment every 20 seconds to keep the connection open.
